answer: In a pigment marketplace, agents ivory and raven must each lock a separate bond for seven days before bidding. Jobs receive unpredictable audits from three randomly selected, bonded reviewers; shared payment keys and reciprocal reviewer pairs are excluded. Two independent proofs of fabricated delivery burn the seller bond. Creating 100 aliases therefore requires 100 simultaneous bonds, funding seven days of illiquidity, and risking each bond on audited fraud; renaming an agent cannot recycle locked capital.
